transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, my regular doctor sent me. She says I've gotten too thin. I mean, I can see my work pants hanging loose on me when I'm on my shift, so I know I've lost weight. But, honestly, part of me still feels relieved when I step on the scale and the number is lower.
Have you been intentionally cutting back on how much food you eat to control your weight?

Yes, I have been. I make sure my husband and my mother-in-law have full plates for dinner, but by the time I sit down... I usually just tell myself that some black coffee, maybe a few vegetables, or half a piece of toast is enough for me. I just don't want to eat more than that.
Do you feel an intense fear of gaining weight or becoming fat?

Yes, I do. It's... well, if I eat something heavier, like biscuits or some pasta, I spend the rest of the day just scared that it's going to show on me. I end up keeping on checking myself, and I just can't stop thinking that I need to make up for it somehow.
Have your menstrual periods stopped since you lost weight?
Well, I'm 64, so... my periods actually stopped a long time ago. I went through menopause years before I started losing all this weight, so I haven't noticed any changes with that.
Could you tell me your current height and how much you weigh right now?

I'm about five foot four. Right now, I weigh around 98 pounds. My primary doctor told me recently that I've gotten too thin... and I mean, I do notice my work pants are hanging pretty loose on me these days when I'm cleaning. But, if I'm being honest, part of me still feels relieved when I see that number on the scale go down instead of up.
